newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates stable, demand higher.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates stable, demand higher.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were unchanged on Thursday, despite strong demand from banks as they awaited a kuna payment from the central bank which bought hard currency at an auction on Wednesday.
The central bank is due to pay 96 million kuna to the banking sector on Friday, used as a voluntary instrument for sterilising money supply.
"The market is very lively and demand is exceptionally high. Banks are seeking all sorts of loans, short and long-term ones," dealer Radmila Nizetic told Reuters.
Midmorning trade by 0900 GMT totalled 33.6 million, but demand for some six million found no lenders. Of this 27 million was call money, steady at 8.0 percent.
Smaller 10-day deals were made at 9.0 percent, while two-week loans were granted at a 10 percent rate. Banks charged 15 percent for 30-day money.
Commercial banks had 109 millon kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, up from Wednesday's 84.1 million, the central bank said.
Overnight trade on Wednesday was negligable as banks had 456 million kuna on their accounts and only one reported a minor shortfall. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
